questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university itself was the most important factor in my decision. Università degli Studi di Milano (UNIMI) offered courses that were relevant to my academic interests, especially within social and political sciences and digital society. It was important to me that the courses aligned well with my degree at UCPH and that they would contribute meaningfully to my academic development. In addition, UNIMI has a good reputation, and Milan is an international city with many opportunities both academically and personally.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find the necessary information upon arrival. UNIMI provided clear instructions through email before arrival, and as long as you followed those instructions carefully, the process was straightforward. Most of the essential steps were explained in advance, which made the transition smoother.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university provided good assistance. There were offices dedicated to Erasmus students, and staff members were available to answer questions either in person, by phone, or via email. They were helpful when dealing with administrative tasks such as registration and documentation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find housing, especially if you start early. There are many student housing options available in Milan, and several online platforms can help. I would recommend starting the search well in advance and making sure to verify the legitimacy of the housing provider.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is very similar to living at home. You have independence and responsibility for your own daily life, including cooking, cleaning, and managing your budget. It is a good way to experience local life more authentically.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process required going in person to the Erasmus office, where staff members, particularly Massimo, assisted with course registration. While the staff were helpful, the process could be somewhat confusing due to differences in scheduling and administrative procedures.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: - You had to go to an address for the office for Erasmus students and then Massimo helped you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You had to visit the Erasmus office physically, where Massimo and his team helped with registering for courses. They provided guidance and assistance, but it required preparation and patience.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not completely successful. Some of the classes I was interested in conflicted with each other in terms of schedule, which made it impossible to take all my preferred courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare well in advance and carefully read all emails and instructions from the university. Course schedules may change, and flexibility is important. It is also helpful to have backup course options prepared.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programme met my expectations overall. The courses were relevant to my field of study, and the level was appropriate.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses matched my expectations and academic background. They were neither too easy nor too difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at UNIMI was more traditional and “old school” compared to UCPH. There was more emphasis on lectures and less interactive discussion. At UCPH, teaching is generally more discussion-based and student-centered, whereas at UNIMI it was more lecture-focused.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would especially recommend Digital Society because the exam format was manageable and interesting, and the content was highly relevant to modern social and digital developments.

questions.answer: I did not participate extensively in organized university activities, so my experience with these was limited.

questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend purchasing a transportation card, which makes it easy and affordable to travel around Milan and nearby areas.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend visiting Lake Como, especially during warmer months. It is beautiful, easy to reach from Milan, and offers a great opportunity to relax and explore nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy to adjust to the local culture. Italians are generally friendly, open, and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The easiest way to meet people is through classes and university activities. Simply talking to classmates and participating in group work helps build connections.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were no major cultural challenges, although the academic system was different.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Italian people have a very positive and relaxed attitude toward life. The social culture, food, and lifestyle were very enjoyable.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Three most important things future students should know:

Search for scholarships and financial support early. Living abroad can be expensive, and financial planning is important.

Be prepared to spend more money than expected, especially on food and daily living.

Do not hesitate to go on exchange. It is a unique and valuable life experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open-minded, flexible, and willing to step outside your comfort zone. An exchange semester is an incredible opportunity for both personal and academic development.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was living in another country and fully experiencing a new culture for an extended period. It helped me grow personally and broaden my perspective.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenge was adapting to the academic system, which was different from UCPH. However, this was also a valuable learning experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
